help: Your full body in VR: its size and posture, the Pip-Boy, the flashlight, two-handed weapons, and smooth movement.

content.text: FRIK brings your full body to Fallout 4 VR. Full-body inverse kinematics move the arms and legs from where your headset and controllers are, so you see your own body, in power armor too.

content.help: Opens the FRIK wiki in your browser. Take off the headset to read it on your monitor.

pages.help: Your body under the headset: its posture, what of it is hidden, the arms, and the world scale.

content.help: Uses the seated postures below in place of the standing ones. Turn it on when you play sitting down.
Where your body is under the headset. Standing, seated, and both in power armor each keep their own values.

content.text: Adjust the body in the game
content.help: Opens FRIK's body adjustment in the game, to set the posture you are in now while you see your body.
How high the headset is above the body. Higher lowers the body under your view.
Raises or lowers the body under the headset.
How much the knees bend. Higher bends them more.
Moves the body forward or back. Lower moves it back, so you do not see into your chest.
How high the headset is above the body. Higher lowers the body under your view.
Raises or lowers the body under the headset.
How much the knees bend. Higher bends them more.
Moves the body forward or back. Lower moves it back, so you do not see into your chest.
How high the headset is above the body. Higher lowers the body under your view.
Raises or lowers the body under the headset.
How much the knees bend. Higher bends them more.
Moves the body forward or back. Lower moves it back, so you do not see into your chest.
How high the headset is above the body. Higher lowers the body under your view.
Raises or lowers the body under the headset.
How much the knees bend. Higher bends them more.
Moves the body forward or back. Lower moves it back, so you do not see into your chest.
The body's height, the knee bend the body adjustment aims for, and comfort sneak.
The height of your body. It scales the skeleton, so a change moves your hands away from where weapons are aligned to them.

warnings.text: Weapons are aligned to the default height.

content.help: The knee bend the body adjustment keeps as it sets the leg slack, so the legs are never straight.
Holds the body at this pitch while comfort sneak lowers you, so the body and what is on it stay in place. 0 for the regular pitch.
What of your head is hidden or moved, so it does not block your view. Hiding a part does not change where you can be hit.
Hides what you wear on your head, as hats and helmets, by the slots Mesh_Hide\slots.ini names.
In selfie mode, shows what the settings of this section hide or move.
Hiding the head and the skin, and moving the head back.
Hides the head, as Mesh_Hide\face.ini names its parts. Your shadow is headless then: Head back offset keeps it.
Hides skin and clothes, as Mesh_Hide\skins.ini names them.
Moves the head back so it does not block your view. Unlike hiding it, it keeps the head's shadow.
How long the arms are, how the elbow bends, and how the shoulder follows the hand.
The length of the arms. Set it so your arms in the game straighten when your own do.
How the arm solver bends the elbow, moves the shoulder, and twists the forearm.
The elbow keeps at least this bend at full reach, so it does not spin when the arm is straight. Try 6 to 14.
The elbow bends at most this much as the hand comes near the shoulder. Past it the upper arm shortens, so the arm does not flip.
The least width of the range in which the wrist's twist steers the elbow, so it still does in a low-ready or a reload.
Blends the elbow where its rules switch, so it does not jump.
How far the shoulder moves toward the hand at full reach, as a part of the arm's length. 0.08 is the original, 0.225 Skyrim VRIK.
Scales how far the shoulder moves down toward the hand. 1 is the original, 0.4 Skyrim VRIK.
Experimental: the part of the upper arm's roll moved to the shoulder's twist bone. Leave at 0 unless you are testing it.

warnings.text: Experimental: it can disturb what other mods read of the body.

content.help: The part of the forearm's roll the bone at the elbow takes. A taper from the elbow, as 0.1, 0.35, 0.55, twists the skin more evenly.
The part of the forearm's roll the middle bone takes.
The part of the forearm's roll the bone at the wrist takes.
Hand damping and elbow smoothing feel the same at any frame rate. Off, they lag more when reprojection halves the frame rate.
How large the world looks to you, which FRIK sets as the game starts.
Sets the world scale below as the game starts. Off leaves fVrScale as Fallout4Custom.ini has it.
How large the world looks, as fVrScale. Higher makes the world look smaller.
Selfie mode and the power armor HUD.
How far in front of you your body is in selfie mode.
Shows the power armor's HUD. Off hides it.

pages.help: The Pip-Boy on your wrist: its model and screen, how it opens and closes, and how you operate it.

content.help: The Pip-Boy model on your wrist.
The size of the Pip-Boy model on your wrist.
Hiding the model, and the model kept with the holo screen.
Hides the Pip-Boy model on your wrist.
With the holo screen, keeps the regular Pip-Boy model on your wrist in place of the holo emitter. The holo screen still opens.
Where the Pip-Boy opens. It is the game's own VR setting, set here for you. FRIK's Pip-Boy is the one on the wrist.

options.help: On your wrist, with FRIK's screen, finger use, and the settings below.
The whole Pip-Boy opens in front of you.
Only the Pip-Boy's screen opens in front of you.

content.text: FRIK's Pip-Boy settings are for the Pip-Boy on the wrist. Set the location to Wrist to change them.

content.help: Where the Pip-Boy's screen is when it opens.
Regular is the screen on the Pip-Boy. Holo is a larger screen that floats above your wrist.

content.text: Adjust the screen in the game
content.help: Opens FRIK's Pip-Boy config in the game, to move the screen and scale the model. Open the Pip-Boy on your wrist first.
When the Pip-Boy opens and closes: as you look at it, or with a button.
Opens the Pip-Boy when you look at it on your wrist.
Closes the Pip-Boy when you look away from it.

content.text: Open button only when looked at
content.help: The open button works only while you look at the Pip-Boy, so it is not opened by accident.
Moving while you do not look at the Pip-Boy closes it at once, without the close delay.
How directly you look, and for how long, for the Pip-Boy to open and close.
How directly you look at the Pip-Boy for it to open. Higher needs a more direct look.
How far you look away from the Pip-Boy for it to close. Lower needs you to look farther away.
How long you look at the Pip-Boy before it opens.
How long you look away from the Pip-Boy before it closes.
How directly you look at the Pip-Boy for the open button to work. Keep it below the look-at threshold.
Steadies the Pip-Boy's screen against the shake of your arm.
How the screen is steadied.

options.help: The screen moves with your wrist, shake and all.
The screen follows your wrist with less shake.
The screen stays where it opened. Hold the hold button to move it.

content.help: When the Pip-Boy moves more than this in a frame, the screen jumps to it in place of lagging behind.
How much the screen's movement is smoothed. Higher is steadier, and lags more.
Using the Pip-Boy with your primary hand: its controller, or your finger.
Scroll and select in the Pip-Boy with the primary hand's controller. The off hand works either way.

content.text: Holster the weapon to use the finger
content.help: Holsters the weapon when you look at the Pip-Boy with the finger in range. Off, holster it yourself, and you need not look.

warnings.text: Players report the weapon holstered by accident, in combat too.

content.help: How near the primary hand comes to the Pip-Boy to point a finger and touch it. 0 turns it off.

pages.help: Holding a weapon with both hands, steadying the hands, and scopes.

content.help: Holding a weapon's barrel with your off hand.
Grip the weapon with your off hand to aim it with both hands.
How your off hand grips the barrel and lets go.

options.help: The hand grips automatically when near the barrel. Move it away quickly to let go.
The hand grips automatically when near the barrel. Press the grip button to let go.
Hold the grip button to grip the barrel. Release it to let go.
Press the grip button to grip the barrel. Press it again to let go.

content.help: How quickly the hand moves away from the barrel to let go. Higher needs a quicker move.
Steadies your hands, so the weapon shakes less.
Steadies the movement of your hands.
Steadies the hands in the game's scope too. Fine aiming is harder then.
How strongly the hands are steadied, out of and in a scope. 0 is none.
How strongly the turning of your hands is steadied. Higher is steadier, and lags more.
How strongly the movement of your hands is steadied. Higher is steadier, and lags more.
How strongly the turning of your hands is steadied in the game's scope.
How strongly the movement of your hands is steadied in the game's scope.
Looking through the game's own scopes.

content.text: Hide the body in a scope
content.help: Hides your body as you look through the game's scope. A scope mod that keeps the body shown, as True Scopes, overrides it.

pages.help: FRIK's flashlight: whether it is used, and where it is on you.

content.help: Turns off FRIK's flashlight, for the game's own or another flashlight mod.
Where the flashlight is. In the game, press grip with a hand near the top of your head to move it to that hand.

pages.help: Smooths the camera's stutter as you move, up and down and from side to side.

content.help: The camera follows the game's movement as it is, without smoothing.
Smoothing of your height, as on stairs and uneven ground.
Higher hides more stutter, and takes longer to come back to your height.
Higher takes longer to come back to your height.
How quickly you come back to your height when you stop. Lower is quicker.
Turns it off indoors, where some players see more jitter.
Smoothing as you move from side to side.
Higher hides more stutter, and slides more when you strafe.
Higher takes longer to come back in line. 0 turns smoothing from side to side off.
How quickly you come back in line when you stop. Lower is quicker.
Turns it off indoors.

pages.help: With Fallout London VR, FRIK keeps its settings in FRIK_FOLVR.toml, and the pages here edit that file. Ignore Fallout London VR stays in FRIK.toml.

content.help: Plays as Fallout 4: FRIK's Pip-Boy works, and FRIK reads FRIK.toml in place of FRIK_FOLVR.toml. It is kept in FRIK.toml.
Grab the Attaboy off your belt to open and close the Pip-Boy.
Pressed with the hand in the zone to open or close the Pip-Boy. Off, the Attaboy opens with the open button anywhere.

pages.help: The controller buttons FRIK listens for.

content.help: Opening, closing and configuring the Pip-Boy on the wrist.
Opens the Pip-Boy.
Closes the Pip-Boy.
Held to move the screen while screen dampening holds it in place.
Gripping a weapon's barrel with your off hand.
Pressed to grip the barrel, and to let go in grip modes 2 and 4.
Held to keep the grip in grip mode 3.
Moving the flashlight between your head and a hand.
Pressed with the left hand near your head to move the flashlight between your head and that hand.
Pressed with the right hand near your head to move the flashlight between your head and that hand.
Opening FRIK's config, and selfie mode.
Opens FRIK's own config in the game. Mods Config FO4 VR takes the button while it is installed.
Turns selfie mode on and off while the Pip-Boy is off.
